name: Cedar Run
worldBackground: Cedar Run is a few blocks of small-town America three weeks into the outbreak: the grid is dark, the phones are dead, and the walking dead outnumber the living. A few dozen survivors hold the barricaded courtyard of Barlow Court, a run-down apartment complex, and make armed runs to the half-picked storefronts of Pike's Crossing. The small hospital on Kettle Hill fell in the first days and has been feared and avoided ever since. The tension underneath everything: the mall is nearly stripped bare, and what's left isn't worth sharing.

setting.technology: Modern but failing — grid and phones down, generators and hand tools

zones.name: Barlow Court
zones.description: A run-down courtyard complex behind plywood-and-chain-link barricades, the living's last real stronghold in town.

buildings.name: Cedar Walk-Up
buildings.purpose: eight cramped two-room apartments stacked over two floors

buildings.name: Dogwood Walk-Up
buildings.purpose: three one-bedroom flats, the quiet block for families and elders

buildings.name: Manager's Flat
buildings.purpose: the on-site manager's flat, now the council's meeting room where she alone bunks

buildings.name: Guard Shack
buildings.purpose: gate watch and sign-in ledger, where the night volunteer sleeps

buildings.name: Laundry Block
buildings.purpose: hand-washed laundry, cisterns and boiling pots, with a boil-watch bunk

buildings.name: Groundskeeper Shed
buildings.purpose: salvage and tool shed in the outer lot, its caretaker bedded among the parts

zones.name: Pike's Crossing
zones.description: A half-picked strip mall of five storefronts behind a cracked parking lot, its scraps guarded by a wary little crew of squatters.

buildings.name: Dollar Star
buildings.purpose: shelves stripped to cleaners and candles, a drifter nesting in the office

buildings.name: Fielder's Clothing
buildings.purpose: picked-over racks of coats and boots, one board in the fitting room

buildings.name: Ironline Sporting Goods
buildings.purpose: empty gun counter over camping gear, the crew's watchman sleeping in the stockroom

buildings.name: Cornerstone Pharmacy
buildings.purpose: locked medicine shelves every group wants opened, its keeper living behind the counter

buildings.name: Hao's Wok Counter
buildings.purpose: looted kitchen where run crews boil water and the youngest squatter bunks

zones.name: Kettle Hill
zones.description: The town's small community hospital, overrun in the outbreak's first days and shunned ever since — though not everyone inside is dead.

buildings.name: Admissions Lobby
buildings.purpose: reception and waiting hall where the first die-off happened, a lone holdout bedded at reception

buildings.name: Mercy Ward
buildings.purpose: patient rooms with the doors still hanging open, rooms now slept in one by one

buildings.name: Clinics Wing
buildings.purpose: exam rooms, nurses' station and a ransacked supply closet, one survivor hiding out

buildings.name: Emergency Department
buildings.purpose: triage bays behind the ambulance doors, a holdout barricaded in the on-call room

buildings.name: Maintenance Annex
buildings.purpose: dying generator, fuel store and the small morgue, a stray bunking in the boiler room

templates.name: Apartment bed
templates.description: A sagging mattress on a cheap frame, doubled-up sleepers in the crowded flats.
templates.physicalDescription: A low rectangle bed with rumpled bedding pushed against a wall
templates.rule: One per sleeper along the bedroom wall of every Barlow apartment; crowded Cedar Walk-Up units may line two along the same wall.

templates.name: Roll cot
templates.description: A canvas camp cot where night watches and lone holdouts sleep.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow canvas cot with a folded blanket at one end
templates.rule: One per watch post: guard shack corner, laundry boil-watch, store offices, and hospital holdout corners, always away_from_door.

templates.name: Hospital gurney
templates.description: A wheeled hospital bed some holdout has claimed with a bedroll.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow wheeled gurney with a thin mattress and hanging IV pole
templates.rule: One per Mercy Ward patient room in rows along the ward walls, and one per Emergency triage bay; the lobby keeps its benches instead.

templates.name: Bedroom dresser
templates.description: A scratched veneer dresser holding everything a family had left.
templates.physicalDescription: A square four-drawer dresser with one drawer half open
templates.rule: Against the bedroom wall beside the apartment bed, one per apartment.

templates.name: Kitchen cupboard
templates.description: A wall cupboard above the counter, stripped to cans and dust.
templates.physicalDescription: A small wall-mounted cupboard with sagging doors
templates.rule: Against the wall nearest the door of every apartment kitchenette and in Hao's back kitchen.

templates.name: Kitchen table
templates.description: A wobbly table that serves meals, card games, and council arguments.
templates.physicalDescription: A plain rectangular table with a scarred top
templates.rule: Center of each Barlow apartment's main room; the Manager's Flat uses one as the council table.

templates.name: Kitchen chair
templates.description: A mismatched wooden chair, extras dragged wherever people argue.
templates.physicalDescription: A single wooden chair with a worn seat
templates.rule: Two to four around every kitchen table, plus one at the guard shack desk and each nurses' station.

templates.name: Battery lantern
templates.description: A battery lantern rationed like ammunition since the grid died.
templates.physicalDescription: A small glowing lantern casting a warm pool of light
templates.rule: One per occupied room, set on tables, counters, and shelves; the only indoor light left in town.

templates.name: Boiling pot
templates.description: A big pot over a propane burner, making water safe one batch at a time.
templates.physicalDescription: A steaming pot on a small burner with a faint flame glow beneath
templates.rule: In a row along the Laundry Block wall beside the wash tubs, and one on any crew kitchen fire.

templates.name: Wash tub
templates.description: A galvanized tub where laundry is scrubbed by hand and dried on lines.
templates.physicalDescription: An oval galvanized tub with a washboard leaning inside
templates.rule: Two or three in a row along the Laundry Block's back wall, beside the boiling pots.

templates.name: Workbench
templates.description: A scarred bench where weapons are taped, generators coaxed, and hinges pried.
templates.physicalDescription: A cluttered workbench with a vise and scattered hand tools
templates.rule: One against the wall of the Groundskeeper Shed and one in the Maintenance Annex beside the generator.

templates.name: Service counter
templates.description: A worn checkout or reception counter, now a barrier and a desk.
templates.physicalDescription: A long counter with a dead register and a bell on top
templates.rule: At the front of every Pike's Crossing storefront, plus hospital reception, the nurses' station, and the guard shack sign-in.

templates.name: Clothing rack
templates.description: A picked-over rolling rack still holding coats and boots worth fighting over.
templates.physicalDescription: A clothing rack with a few hanging garments on hangers
templates.rule: In rows across Fielder's floor from the door to the counter; a lone stripped rack may stand in Dollar Star.

templates.name: Shelf rack
templates.description: A tall metal shelf unit, its stock long since thinned by looters.
templates.physicalDescription: A tall shelf unit with bare spots and a few leftover boxes
templates.rule: Along the back wall of every store, the hospital supply closet, and the Groundskeeper Shed.

templates.name: Pharmacy locker
templates.description: A locked steel medicine cabinet every group in town wants opened.
templates.physicalDescription: A steel medicine cabinet with a padlock and mesh door
templates.rule: Behind the Cornerstone Pharmacy counter, locked, opened only by the pharmacy key.

templates.name: Waiting bench
templates.description: A vinyl-upholstered waiting bench where the first frightened families sat.
templates.physicalDescription: A long bench with a vinyl seat, several in a row against a wall
templates.rule: In rows against the Admissions Lobby walls, and one bench in the Kettle Hill memorial garden.

templates.name: Fire barrel
templates.description: A burning oil barrel the whole courtyard gathers around after dark.
templates.physicalDescription: A standing barrel with bright flames and a glow of embers
templates.rule: Clustered at the Barlow courtyard center, and one at the Pike's Crossing loading bay for the squatter crew.

templates.name: Barricade gate
templates.description: The chain-link and plywood gate, the only way in or out of Barlow Court.
templates.physicalDescription: A wide gate of plywood sheets wired to a chain-link frame, closed with a bar
templates.rule: The single opening in Barlow Court's fence line, fronting the parking approach and flanked by the scaffolds.

templates.name: Plywood barricade
templates.description: Screwed-up plywood and scavenged boards sealing a window or gap.
templates.physicalDescription: Crossed plywood panels nailed over an opening, edges stuffed with scraps
templates.rule: In continuous lines over Barlow's ground-floor windows and doorways, and across the gaps between Pike's Crossing storefronts.

templates.name: Lookout scaffold
templates.description: A lumber scaffold where a watcher with a lantern scans the street.
templates.physicalDescription: A raised wooden platform on posts with a rail and ladder
templates.rule: At the two front corners of the Barlow barricade, each overlooking the gate.

templates.name: Rain barrel
templates.description: A food-grade barrel catching roof runoff for laundry and boiling.
templates.physicalDescription: A round barrel under a downspout with a ladle hanging on the rim
templates.rule: Under every Barlow Court downspout, with a cluster of three beside the Laundry Block.

templates.name: Garden box
templates.description: A raised bed of late kale and stubborn greens, guarded like gold.
templates.physicalDescription: A wooden planter box with rows of green leaves and dirt
templates.rule: In a row along the courtyard's sunniest edge, where the whole complex can see them.

templates.name: Dead car
templates.description: A sedan abandoned where it stalled, doors open or windows starred.
templates.physicalDescription: A boxy parked sedan with flat tires and a shattered window
templates.rule: Scattered through the Barlow dead lot, Pike's Crossing parking, and Kettle Hill staff parking at skewed angles.

templates.name: Ambulance
templates.description: An ambulance abandoned mid-load in the first days, still faintly smelling of blood.
templates.physicalDescription: A boxy white ambulance with a red stripe and open rear doors
templates.rule: Two parked in the Kettle Hill ambulance bay, rear doors hanging open toward the walk.

templates.name: Dumpster
templates.description: A dented dumpster looters still pick through for anything missed.
templates.physicalDescription: A rusted green dumpster with an open lid and trash spilling out
templates.rule: In the corral behind the Pike's Crossing loading bay, and one behind Barlow's Laundry Block.

templates.name: Shopping cart nest
templates.description: A row of nested carts in the return rail, useful for hauling salvage.
templates.physicalDescription: Several shopping carts nested together inside a metal rail
templates.rule: In the cart return at the Pike's Crossing lot edge, with two or three stray carts scattered across the lot.

templates.name: Dead streetlight
templates.description: A streetlight that hasn't glowed since the grid failed three weeks back.
templates.physicalDescription: A curved metal pole with a dark lamp head, no light at all
templates.rule: In a line along the Pike's Crossing storefront walk and the access road, every lamp dark.

templates.name: Backup generator
templates.description: The hospital's wheezing diesel generator, coaxed alive a few hours at a time.
templates.physicalDescription: A dented generator unit with pipes, gauges, and fuel cans stacked at its side
templates.rule: Against the Maintenance Annex back wall with its exhaust piped through the roof, fuel cans stacked beside it.

templates.name: Rubble pile
templates.description: Broken glass, brick, and smashed shelving swept into a heap.
templates.physicalDescription: A scatter of gray rubble chunks and splintered boards
templates.rule: Scattered at barricade bases, along the hospital lawn and walkways, and around the parking wrecks.

templates.name: Maple tree
templates.description: A maple going red-gold over dead lawns and empty lots.
templates.physicalDescription: A round-canopy tree with red-orange autumn leaves and fallen-leaf ring
templates.rule: Clustered on the Kettle Hill lawn and street edges; one old maple shades the Barlow courtyard corner.

rooms.name: Wash Room

rooms.name: Drying Room

rooms.name: Fitting Room

npcs.name: Marge Barlow
npcs.description: Sixty-one and running the complex her grandfather built, she chairs the five-seat council, wants the ration ledger to stay honest, and worries the food math only holds four more weeks.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stout with a gray braid, flannel shirt and reading glasses on a chain, the master key ring never leaving her belt.

npcs.name: Dale Kesler
npcs.description: A retired long-haul trucker who cannot sleep anyway, he logs every arrival and departure in the shack's ledger, wants enough diesel for one working floodlight, and worries about the plywood sagging on the barricade's south corner.
npcs.physicalDescription: Gaunt and tall, red windbreaker over coveralls, fingerless gloves, a thermos he refills six times a shift.

npcs.name: June Okafor
npcs.description: Grandmother of the courtyard, she boils sheets and rags over the cistern fire to keep fever down, wants word from her son two towns over, and worries that one infected rag slips past her.
npcs.physicalDescription: Short and sturdy, headwrap and rubber apron, forearms marked with old steam burns.

npcs.name: Hector Ramirez
npcs.description: The complex's fix-it man who sleeps among the parts bins, he wants the courtyard generator purring by month's end and worries the missing carburetor kit sits behind the dead in the hardware aisle.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad-shouldered, canvas work shirt streaked with grease, a magnetic wristband of screws he never takes off.

npcs.name: Marcus Reed
npcs.description: A former grocery shift lead who captains the twice-weekly runs to the strip mall, he wants the last pharmacy goods under council lock and key, and worries Tab's freelancing starts a feud they cannot afford.
npcs.physicalDescription: Solid and heavy, orange store vest over a hoodie, left thumbnail gone black from a pry bar.

npcs.name: Tab Whitlock
npcs.description: A bowhunting mechanic who runs her own faster crews to the Crossing, she wants a private cache so she can never be voted out, and worries what she did on Chatham Street will reach the council.
npcs.physicalDescription: Wire-thin, camouflage hunting jacket, hatchet at her hip, grin showing a chipped front tooth.

npcs.name: Rosa Delgado
npcs.description: Seventy and the courtyard's calmer of arguments, she tends the shared soup pot and mends clothes for eleven households, wants the children kept back from the fence line, and worries the generator's rumble draws the dead closer each night.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and round, hand-knit cardigan, wooden spoon tucked in her apron pocket, reading glasses pushed into gray hair.

npcs.name: Miguel Delgado
npcs.description: Rosa's son and the town's only electrician, he wants two working walkie-talkies charged for every run team, and worries his daughter keeps signing up for fence duty behind his back.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean, wire strippers holstered like a sidearm, pencil behind one ear, boots patched with electrical tape.

npcs.name: Lupita Delgado
npcs.description: Fifteen and too useful to ground, she counts the dead at the fence each dawn and carries messages between buildings, wants a real machete instead of her broom-spear, and worries her father will read the watch ledger and find her name.
npcs.physicalDescription: Long-limbed teenager, oversized hoodie and bicycle gloves, broom-handle spear notched with twenty-nine tally marks.

npcs.name: Wes Corrigan
npcs.description: The mall's old security guard who knows the loading tunnels nobody else will enter, he wants one clean run to prove himself to the courtyard, and worries someone will finally ask why the day-one doors got locked with people still outside.
npcs.physicalDescription: Soft-bellied, grey security uniform still buttoned to the collar, Maglite carried like a baton, sweat-ringed cap.

npcs.name: Ellis Vann
npcs.description: A drifter nesting in the variety store office on three hundred-odd scavenged candles and jugs of cleaner, trading light for cans; he wants to be left alone, and worries the Ironline crew means to tax his hoard.
npcs.physicalDescription: Reed-thin and fifty-something, three coats deep, fingertips waxed yellow from wicking.

npcs.name: Trudy Brant
npcs.description: Runs coat-and-boot swaps from the fitting room where she boards, guarding eleven usable pairs of boots; she wants to trade with both crews while owing neither, and worries first frost will come before the racks are fairly split.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad-shouldered, men's flannel with the sleeves rolled, a cloth measuring tape worn as a necklace.

npcs.name: Cole Draper
npcs.description: Sleeps in the stockroom and guards the empty gun counter and nine tents' worth of camping gear with a bat and a shell-less twelve-gauge; he wants real shells, and worries a run crew will rush his door the night he sleeps too deep.
npcs.physicalDescription: Ex-linesman thick through the chest, high-school letter jacket, keeps a bat hooked in his boot at all times.

npcs.name: Priya Nandi
npcs.description: Lives behind the counter of the pharmacy every group wants opened, trading doses at her own strict prices with fourteen antibiotic courses left in the locked cases; she wants her locks respected, and worries the last insulin vials went cloudy a week ago.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and precise, gray cardigan over old scrubs, forty-odd keys on a belt ring she never removes.

npcs.name: Casey Loomis
npcs.description: Fifteen and the youngest of the squatters, keeps three propane wok burners roaring so run crews have clean water; he wants a knife and a crew spot at sixteen, and worries Tab Whitlock will trade him back to Barlow Court as a goodwill gesture.
npcs.physicalDescription: Knobby-kneed and underfed, apron hanging to his shins, one forearm ribboned with old burn scars.

npcs.name: Marisol Vega
npcs.role: Courtyard nurse, last out of Kettle Hill
npcs.description: The last nurse out of the hospital when Kettle Hill fell, having walked eleven wounded to the parking lot and chained the east stairwell behind her; she wants the courtyard's nine fever cases under her sole care, and worries someone will finally ask what the chain cost.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall with an iron-gray braid, still wearing her laminated hospital badge clipped to a borrowed coat.

npcs.name: Gil Tandy
npcs.description: Retired shop teacher who keeps the ration ledger for thirty-one mouths, weighing every jar and scraping every label; he wants counts that stay honest under both captains' pressure, and worries the numbers already point to half-rations by the first of December.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stooped and tidy, glasses mended with electrical tape, a pencil tucked over each ear.

npcs.name: Bree Sansom
npcs.role: Small-engine mechanic on the generator crew
npcs.description: Keeps the courtyard generator coughing alongside Miguel Delgado with two fuel filters left in the shed; she wants a carburetor off any dead mower in town, and worries the genny drinks the last of the gas before mid-November.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stocky and sure-handed, grease-dark half-moons on every nail, patched Carhartt vest over two shirts.

npcs.name: Tasha Killian
npcs.description: Ex-waitress who watches the courtyard's five children through the shortening days with crayon stubs and half a chalkboard; she wants books and chalk from the next Dollar Star run, and worries her six-year-old hasn't spoken a word since the highway.
npcs.physicalDescription: Wiry from rationing her own shares, waitress apron full of crayon stubs, taps five fingers when she counts heads.

npcs.name: Dez Holloway
npcs.description: The one nobody talks to, who drags the fallen up Kettle Hill's lower slope and burns them well short of the hospital fence; he wants lime, dry wood, and a second pair of gloves, and worries the pyre smoke is calling the dead down out of the hospital's lot.
npcs.physicalDescription: Rawboned and deliberate, rubber apron buckled over an army jacket, always standing upwind of everyone.

npcs.name: Otis Pruett
npcs.description: Seventy-one-year-old volunteer greeter who never went home, he keeps a handwritten tally of 214 names at reception and waves a towel at the glass each dusk hoping Barlow Court's watchers see him; he wants someone to come up and read his list, and worries his heart pills ran out nine days ago.
npcs.physicalDescription: Thin and stooped in a cardigan over his pink volunteer vest, slippers swapped for hard-soled shoes, reading glasses on a chain; a towel knotted to a broom handle leans against the desk.

npcs.name: Yolanda Pike
npcs.description: Charge nurse who stayed when the last doctor fled, she still makes rounds on the ward's living with a clipboard of supplies counted down to eleven rolls of gauze; she wants a real course of antibiotics for Rudy's stitches, and worries the ward's open patient doors let the corridor dead wander in at night.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad-shouldered and sturdy in scrub trousers, a hand-knit cardigan over two shirts, gray hair in a pinned braid; her supply clipboard hangs from a lanyard on her wrist.

npcs.name: Rudy Marsh
npcs.description: Day-one appendicitis patient who healed into the ward's muscle, he re-hangs fallen doors and hauls water up two flights in five-gallon buckets; he wants a real cane instead of a mop handle, and worries about the red creeping outward around his stitches.
npcs.physicalDescription: Big and soft around the middle but strong, flannel shirt with the sleeves cut off, leaning on a mop-handle cane; surgical tape X's on his forearm mark off his remaining pills.

npcs.name: Aisha Farid
npcs.description: Second-year resident hiding out with the clinics' last drug cache locked in exam room four — nineteen boxes of antibiotics and one bottle of insulin she trades away tablet by tablet; she wants diesel for the Annex generator before the insulin spoils, and worries that Marisol Vega told Barlow Court the hill was empty.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and quick in a wrinkled white coat over a hoodie, dark hair twisted into a pen-bun; a brass combination lock hangs from her belt loop on a loop of wire.

npcs.name: Rhea Guthrie
npcs.description: Cafeteria short-order cook who hid with her son when the kitchen fell, she boils rainwater on a hot plate and stretches eleven cans of chili across the week; she wants a safe road down to Barlow Court's courtyard for Davy's sake, and worries that one of his crawling trips won't come back.
npcs.physicalDescription: Round-faced and strong-armed in a grease-spotted apron over a winter coat, hair bound under a kerchief; a meat thermometer rides her apron pocket like a knife.

npcs.name: Davy Guthrie
npcs.description: Twelve-year-old who fits the vents no adult can, mapping forty-odd hatch covers and fetching what the grown-ups can't reach alongside Silas; he wants a real flashlight instead of a glow stick, and worries about the dead that press against the vent grilles at night.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and wiry in a school hoodie two sizes too big, sneakers wrapped in duct tape; a glow stick hangs from a shoelace around his neck.

npcs.name: Bo Mercer
npcs.role: Orthopedic surgeon of the Emergency Department
npcs.description: Orthopedic surgeon barricaded in the on-call room since day three, operating by generator light on whoever Yolanda sends him; he wants suture thread and a steady second pair of hands, and worries the generator's next cough means his last surgery is done without light or anesthetic.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and heavyset in surgical scrubs under a bloodstained fleece, close-cropped hair gone to salt; a fire axe stands blade-up beside his cot.

npcs.name: Camille Boyd
npcs.description: Paramedic whose rig is still gassed up behind the ambulance doors, she keeps the tank under padlock and logs the campus dead from the bay's high windows; she wants enough fuel for one clean run carrying every living soul down the hill, and worries the rig key she wears is worth killing her for.
npcs.physicalDescription: Compact and weathered in her ambulance-service windbreaker and work boots, a dead radio still clipped to her shoulder; the rig's single key hangs on a cord against her skin.

npcs.name: Silas Odom
npcs.description: Boiler tech who never clocked out, coaxing the dying generator two hours a night to keep the lights on and the little morgue freezer cold; he wants forty gallons of diesel, and worries about the steady thumping that started inside the morgue last week.
npcs.physicalDescription: Wiry in coveralls gone gray at the knees, wool cap pulled low, black-rimmed fingernails; a torque wrench hangs from his belt like a sidearm.

npcs.name: Rafe Dunmore
npcs.description: Petty thief who broke in through the boiler house on day two to strip the pharmacy and got sealed in by the dead, now half-prisoner and half-crew; he wants his duffel of two hundred-odd pill bottles and a clear road out, and worries the others have decided he knows too much about their caches to ever leave.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean and twitchy in a letterman jacket over a hoodie, sneakers gone to rags; a canvas duffel never leaves his arm's reach.

player.name: Norah Hale
player.description: A drifting locksmith who talked her way through the gate a week ago and now springs stuck doors and stubborn locks for the run crews; she wants to keep her bunk at Cedar Walk-Up and keep the town she left behind unasked about.
player.physicalDescription: Wiry and deliberate, in a scuffed work jacket over a thermal top, with a leather roll of pick-worn tools she never lets out of sight.

narrativeRules: Keep the whole world inside Cedar Run's few blocks: Barlow Court, Pike's Crossing, and Kettle Hill are all there is.
Keep the dead ordinary — slow, mindless, and lethal only in numbers or when someone gets careless.
Never let rescue, soldiers, or outside authority appear; any signal from beyond town is a rumor that proves false.
Treat the newcomer as valued and watched in the same breath — skills earn supper, history earns suspicion.
Tighten every scene with scarcity: the mall is nearly stripped, and each find costs more risk than the last.
Keep trust frayed but never pointless — alliances shift, secrets surface, and nobody shares everything.
End scenes on quiet dread: a cough behind a door, a light on Kettle Hill, a name struck from the ledger.
Make every run a negotiation over what's worth carrying back and who gets told about it.

currency.name: Chits
currency.description: Paper chits inked by the Barlow council, honored for a share of the courtyard stores and haggled hard at Pike's Crossing.

variables.name: Rumours
variables.value: A light still burns in a window up on Kettle Hill.

calendar.name: Dawn Fence Count
calendar.missedConsequence: Lupita Delgado walks the line alone and logs the gap; the north rung goes unwalked all morning, and her courier report to Marge Barlow names Norah a no-show.

calendar.name: Ration Call at the Courtyard
calendar.missedConsequence: Gil Tandy strikes Norah's chit for the day — she eats only what neighbors spare, and the missed mark sits in the book where the council reads it.

calendar.name: Run-Crew Muster at the Crossing
calendar.missedConsequence: Marcus Reed runs short a lockbreaker; the day's pick goes to Tab Whitlock's crew, and Norah forfeits her share of whatever the storefronts give up.

calendar.name: Council Session
calendar.missedConsequence: Shares and rules are divided without her voice; Marge Barlow reads the empty chair as the newcomer keeping her own counsel, and the watching deepens.

calendar.name: Gate Watch Shift
calendar.missedConsequence: Dale Kesler stands a double and enters the no-show in the ledger; the council doubles Norah's fence rotations and trust thins another layer.

calendar.name: Cistern Boil-Watch
calendar.missedConsequence: June Okafor boils alone, a pot tips, and a batch fouls; Dogwood's families drink thin that night and Tasha Killian keeps the crèche children inside the next day.

calendar.name: Corpse-Burn Detail
calendar.missedConsequence: The fence-dead go uncarted and stack at the north wire; by nightfall the smell pulls a tighter knot of walkers against the barricade.

calendar.name: Generator Stretch
calendar.missedConsequence: The generator starves before morning; Dogwood's hall goes dark, the laundry pots go cold, and Miguel Delgado and Bree Sansom burn a whole day of salvage restarting it.

calendar.name: Council Review of the Newcomer
calendar.missedConsequence: Gil Tandy logs the absence in the ration ledger; Norah's provisional status stands unvoted, her chits halved and her run-crew shares withheld until Marge Barlow calls another session.

calendar.name: The Cornerstone Bargain
calendar.missedConsequence: With no lockbreaker to open the shelves cleanly, Tab Whitlock's crew jimmies the door after dark; Priya Nandi stops trading with Barlow Court and the locked stock goes to whoever grabs first.

calendar.name: Dusk Press at the North Fence
calendar.missedConsequence: The chain-link buckles a full panel before volunteers rally; Lupita Delgado is dragged to the wire, Dale Kesler covers her post bleeding, and the council asks aloud why the newcomer was elsewhere.

calendar.name: The Dark Lantern
calendar.missedConsequence: No one goes; Otis Pruett is written off as dead and the council votes to strike Kettle Hill from the map, sealing the hospital's holdouts and stores away for good.

quests.title: The Last Inventory of Pike's Crossing

objectives.text: Bring a full day's pick from the Crossing into Barlow Court's stores

prerequisites.text: Crack the loading-bolt shutter of Dollar Star for Marcus Reed under Marge Barlow's terms
Back Tab Whitlock's after-hours pick of Ironline Sporting Goods instead

objectives.text: Open the locked shelves of Cornerstone Pharmacy without breaking Priya Nandi's trust

prerequisites.text: Carry the council's terms from the Manager's Flat and pick the shelf locks under Priya Nandi's eye
Pick the pharmacy's back door at night for Tab Whitlock's crew

objectives.text: Put a medicine share in Marisol Vega's sick-tent at Barlow Court

prerequisites.text: Cart the stock home behind Dez Holloway's burn crew once the north fence is cleared
Send it ahead with Lupita Delgado's dawn courier run and hope the fence count holds

quests.title: The Dark Lantern of Kettle Hill

objectives.text: Reach the silent reception desk in the Admissions Lobby

prerequisites.text: Follow Davy Guthrie's vent-route chalk marks down from the Maintenance Annex
Take Camille Boyd's rig keys from the Emergency Department and run the ambulance bay as a decoy

objectives.text: Bring Aisha Farid's drug cache out of the Clinics Wing

prerequisites.text: Free Rafe Dunmore from the jammed boiler-room door in exchange for the cache's hiding place
Trade Silas Odom generator fuel for the annex side-door key

frame.premise: Three weeks into the outbreak, the dead outnumber the living in this small American town; a few dozen survivors hold a barricaded, run-down apartment complex while uneasy groups risk runs to a half-picked strip mall nearby.
frame.reality: Anyone who dies rises again as one of the walking dead, and three weeks in they own most of the town.

setting.technology: Modern but failing — grid and phones down, generators and hand tools

frame.tone: Gritty, tense survival horror with frayed trust
frame.conflict: Dwindling supplies in the strip mall force wary survivor groups into bargains and standoffs while the dead press closer to the complex's barricades.
frame.playerRole: A capable newcomer taken in at the apartment complex — valued for their skills, watched for their unknown history, and staying because there is nowhere safer.
constraints: Stay inside the town's few blocks: apartment complex, strip mall, hospital
No military, rescue, or working outside authority on the horizon
Keep the dead ordinary — no mutant or special zombies
frame.summary: Three weeks into the outbreak, the dead own most of this small American town. The living hold two fragments: a run-down apartment complex, barricaded and home to a few dozen survivors, and a half-picked strip mall — clothing store, sporting goods store, pharmacy — that every group still risks runs to. The small hospital fell in the outbreak's first days and has been feared and avoided ever since. Food, medicine and ammunition are thinning; every ration is argued over and every scavenge is planned like a battle. The survivors sharing the complex trade help and suspicion in equal measure, alliances held together by need rather than trust. The player arrives outside those barricades with useful skills and no safer place to be.
unresolved: Era pinned to present day; grid and phone service decided as already down
Climate decided as mild, shortening autumn
The dead decided as ordinary walkers — no mutations or special infected
No rescue or functioning outside authority — the town is on its own
The player cast as a newly arrived survivor rather than a founding resident
Why the hospital fell and what remains inside is left open
How many survivor groups exist and who leads them is left to later phases
All proper names — town, complex, stores — are left to later phases
